title: HealthRing tier colors (green/orange/red) + tests
instructions:
MODIFY the existing `HealthRing` component and its test file (both are provided as context files). One behavior change: the FILLED segment color now depends on the character's health ratio. Everything else about the component (segment math, layout, props, center label, data attributes) stays EXACTLY as it is.

## FILES TO EMIT (exactly these two paths — complete rewrites of the context files)

1. `client/src/ui/HealthRing.tsx`
2. `client/src/ui/HealthRing.test.tsx`

## Component change — HealthRing.tsx

Add, right after the existing `const fontSize = ...` line and before the `segmentCircles` loop:

```tsx
// Health-tier coloring: red at or below 1/3 max HP, orange at or below 1/2,
// green above. Integer comparisons (hp*3 <= maxHp) avoid float rounding.
const critical = hp * 3 <= maxHp;
const warning = hp * 2 <= maxHp;
const tier = critical ? 'critical' : warning ? 'warn' : 'ok';
const fillColor = tier === 'critical' ? '#ef4444' : tier === 'warn' ? '#fb923c' : '#4ade80';
```

In the svg root element, add one attribute next to the existing data-* attributes:

```tsx
data-tier={tier}
```

In the segment circle loop, change the stroke line from:

```tsx
stroke={isFilled ? '#4ade80' : 'rgba(255,255,255,0.12)'}
```

to:

```tsx
stroke={isFilled ? fillColor : 'rgba(255,255,255,0.12)'}
```

Empty segments keep the same grey `rgba(255,255,255,0.12)` at every tier. Do not change anything else: same imports, same props interface (hp, maxHp, size?, strokeWidth?), same math lines, same JSX structure, same class names (`health-ring`, `health-ring-label`, `health-segment`, `health-filled`, `health-empty`), same aria-label. No classes, no default exports, no mutation.

## Test change — HealthRing.test.tsx

Keep ALL existing tests unchanged (they assert data-segments/data-filled/class counts and still hold). Then ADD a new describe block `describe('HealthRing tiers', () => { ... });` with these cases (same imports; the `countOf` helper already exists in the file):

1. it('full health: green segments, tier ok'):
   `const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<HealthRing hp={90} maxHp={90} />);`
   - expect html to contain `data-tier="ok"`
   - expect `countOf(html, 'stroke="#4ade80"')` to be 9

2. it('exactly half health: orange, tier warn'):
   `const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<HealthRing hp={45} maxHp={90} />);`
   - expect html to contain `data-tier="warn"`
   - expect html to contain `stroke="#fb923c"`
   - expect html NOT to contain `stroke="#4ade80"`
   - expect `countOf(html, 'stroke="#fb923c"')` to be 5 (filled segments: Math.round(4.5) = 5... use `Math.round(45/10)` semantics — 45/10 = 4.5 rounds to 5, but JS Math.round(4.5) is 5)

3. it('just above half: green, tier ok'):
   `const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<HealthRing hp={46} maxHp={90} />);`
   - expect html to contain `data-tier="ok"`
   - expect html to contain `stroke="#4ade80"`

4. it('exactly one third: red, tier critical'):
   `const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<HealthRing hp={30} maxHp={90} />);`
   - expect html to contain `data-tier="critical"`
   - expect html to contain `stroke="#ef4444"`
   - expect html NOT to contain `stroke="#fb923c"`
   - expect html NOT to contain `stroke="#4ade80"`

5. it('just above one third: orange, tier warn'):
   `const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<HealthRing hp={31} maxHp={90} />);`
   - expect html to contain `data-tier="warn"`

6. it('zero health: red'):
   `const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<HealthRing hp={0} maxHp={80} />);`
   - expect html to contain `data-tier="critical"`
   - no filled segments, so expect html NOT to contain `stroke="#ef4444"` — the tier attribute still reports critical

7. it('empty segments stay grey at every tier'):
   `const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<HealthRing hp={30} maxHp={90} />);`
   - expect `countOf(html, 'stroke="rgba(255,255,255,0.12)"')` to be 6 (3 filled red, 6 empty grey of 9 segments)

Serializer facts: React renders the stroke attribute verbatim (`stroke="#fb923c"`), including inside the rgba string. `data-tier={tier}` serializes to `data-tier="ok"` / `data-tier="warn"` / `data-tier="critical"`.

NOTE on case 2's expected count: filled = Math.min(segments, Math.max(0, Math.round(hp / 10))). For hp 45: Math.round(4.5) = 5 in JavaScript (half rounds up), so 5 filled segments each carry the orange stroke. For case 7 (hp 30, maxHp 90): Math.round(3) = 3 filled, 9 - 3 = 6 empty.

## VALIDATION (both must pass)

- in `client/`: `npx tsc --noEmit`
- in `client/`: `npx vitest run` (the FULL client suite)
